name: Barbados

most.note: Check when you last had a tetanus, diphtheria and polio booster. If it was more than ten years ago and you'll be anywhere medical care is limited, a booster is recommended.

some.note: Spread by daytime-biting mosquitoes. The vaccine is worth discussing for longer stays and for anyone at higher risk; bite avoidance matters for everyone.
Spread by daytime-biting mosquitoes, and bite avoidance is the main protection. Ask about the vaccine if you've had dengue before.
Recommended for most people going to Barbados who haven't had it before. It spreads through food and water, and a good hotel doesn't remove the risk.
Worth considering if you'll be around animals, in rural areas or far from medical care, and for children, who are bitten more often. The course takes three or four weeks, so book early.

certificates: A yellow fever certificate is asked for from travellers aged 1 year and over arriving from a country with yellow fever risk. Flying straight from the UK, you won't need one.
